name: Front Pads
description: Friction material. The single biggest tuning item for a race car: pick a race compound with a temperature window that matches the car (a 3,700+ lb Camaro on slicks needs a high-temp endurance pad). Factory ZL1 Brembo pads are ~15.8 mm thick; AP CP9668 pads are 25 mm.

components.name: Front brake pads (set per axle)
components.description: One pad set per caliper (2 pads each). Race pads need more heat to work, generate more dust, and must be bedded. Run different compounds front/rear to tune bias if needed.
components.location: Inside each front caliper, either side of the rotor.

factory.name: GM/Brembo ZL1 front pads (ZL1 1LE shape)
factory.notes: OEM thickness ≈ 15.8 mm (forum-measured). Banned for sale in CA/WA early on (copper content) per Wikipedia.

installNotes: Push pistons back with fluid level watched (siphon reservoir first).
Lube backing-plate ears, fit pins/clips, pump pedal before moving the car.
inspection: Measure every session: replace at ~3–4 mm friction remaining (or 50% for endurance stints).
Look for taper (leading/trailing) > 1 mm – indicates caliper flex or piston size mismatch.
Check for cracks, glazing, delamination from backing plate.

components.name: Front pad thermal shims / heat barriers
components.description: Titanium or ceramic-backed shims between pad backing plate and pistons reduce heat soak into the caliper and fluid – cheap insurance against fluid boil on a heavy car.
components.location: Between each pad backing plate and the pistons.
installNotes: Fit with each new pad set if pad thickness tolerance allows.
